# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group - 1,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, "per group:", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Additional validation using base R t-distribution
# Non-centrality parameter for one-sided test
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) * d = sqrt(n/2) * d for equal n
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2)
power_base_r <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Verification using base R t-distribution:\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", round(lambda, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(t_crit, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - Type II error):", round(power_base_r, 4), "\n\n")

# Output in structured format
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "participants\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  sample_size_per_group = n_per_group,
  total_sample_size = n_per_group * 2,
  achieved_power = round(power_achieved, 4),
  power_preceding_design = round(power_preceding, 4),
  continuous_solution = round(result$n, 3),
  cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 4),
  lambda = round(lambda, 4),
  verification_power = round(power_base_r, 4)
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * 2, unit = "participants"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(result$n, 3), unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), sep = "")

# Independent verification of two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# Design: One-sided test, H0: μ1 = μ2 vs H1: μ1 > μ2 (or similar directional)
# Given: delta = 4.3 dBA, sd_common = 7.8 dBA, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

library(pwr)

# Input parameters
delta <- 4.3
sd_common <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 6), "\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation: 1:1\n\n")

# Method 1: Using pwr.t.test with alternative='greater'
result_greater <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("Method 1 - pwr.t.test(alternative='greater'):\n")
cat("Continuous solution (n per group):", round(result_greater$n, 6), "\n")
cat("Minimum integer (ceiling):", ceiling(result_greater$n), "\n\n")

# Method 2: Manual calculation using non-centrality parameter
# For two-sample t-test with equal n per group:
# Non-centrality = d * sqrt(n_total / 2) = d * sqrt(n_per_group)
# df = n_total - 2 = 2*n - 2
# Critical value: t_alpha = qt(1 - alpha, df)
# Power = 1 - P(T < t_alpha | ncp = non_centrality)

cat("Method 2 - Manual NCP approach:\n")

# Function to compute power given n per group
compute_power_manual <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha) {
  n_total <- 2 * n_per_group
  df <- n_total - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n_per_group)  # sqrt(n_per_group) because sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) = sqrt(n/2)*sqrt(2) = sqrt(n)
  # Actually, ncp = d * sqrt((n1*n2)/(n1+n2)) = d * sqrt(n^2/(2n)) = d * sqrt(n/2)
  ncp_correct <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp_correct)
  return(power)
}

# Verify power at n=42
power_at_42 <- compute_power_manual(42, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=42 per group:", round(power_at_42, 6), "\n")

# Verify power at n=41
power_at_41 <- compute_power_manual(41, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=41 per group:", round(power_at_41, 6), "\n\n")

# Method 3: Using pwr.t.test to verify power at specific n values
verify_42 <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, n = 42, sig.level = alpha,

cat("Power at n=41:", round(verify_41$power, 6), "\n\n")

# Cross-check with uniroot to find exact minimum n for target power
find_min_n <- function(target_power_val, d, alpha) {
  lower_n <- 1
  upper_n <- 200
  
  # Binary search
  while (upper_n - lower_n > 0.01) {
    mid_n <- (lower_n + upper_n) / 2
    power_mid <- compute_power_manual(mid_n, d, alpha)

    } else {

    }
  }
  return((lower_n + upper_n) / 2)
}

# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group - 1,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, "per group:", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Additional validation using base R t-distribution
# Non-centrality parameter for one-sided test
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) * d = sqrt(n/2) * d for equal n

# Method 2: Manual calculation using non-centrality parameter
# For two-sample t-test with equal n per group:
# Non-centrality = d * sqrt(n_total / 2) = d * sqrt(n_per_group)
# df = n_total - 2 = 2*n - 2
# Critical value: t_alpha = qt(1 - alpha, df)
# Power = 1 - P(T < t_alpha | ncp = non_centrality)

cat("Method 2 - Manual NCP approach:\n")

# Function to compute power given n per group
compute_power_manual <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha) {
  n_total <- 2 * n_per_group
  df <- n_total - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n_per_group)  # sqrt(n_per_group) because sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) = sqrt(n/2)*sqrt(2) = sqrt(n)
  # Actually, ncp = d * sqrt((n1*n2)/(n1+n2)) = d * sqrt(n^2/(2n)) = d * sqrt(n/2)
  ncp_correct <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp_correct)
  return(power)
}

  lower_n <- 1

    }

  return((lower_n + upper_n) / 2)
}

# Evidence e1; success=false

# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
